 Sébastien Lecornu suggests more curfews could be introduced to quell unrest after weekend protests

 37s ago 05.44 EDT Agreements on sanitary rules, emissions trading systems, youth experience among priorities for upcoming UK summit, EU commissioner says
 Jakub Krupa EU trade commissioner Maroš Šefčovič said the bloc’s relationship with the UK is of “vital importance in the current geopolitical, security and economic context,” as he set out the bloc’s expectations ahead of next month’s EU-UK summit on 20 November.
 View image in fullscreen EU trade commissioner Maroš Šefčovič speaks during a debate on 'EU–UK summit: renewed ambition for a closer partnership' at the European parliament in Strasbourg, France. Photograph: Ronald Wittek/EPA Speaking at the European parliament in Strasbourg minutes after holding a phone call with UK’s Europe minister Hamish Falconer , he said the EU had three priorities for any talks with London. 
 Crucially, he wanted the two sides to fully implement the existing agreements, which include the protection of six million EU citizens resident in the UK and about a million UK nationals in the EU.
 “We must ensure they can fully enjoy their rights now and in the future. That is why we continue to push for solutions on all matters affecting them,” he said.
 He also said that “the work continues” on implementing the Windsor framework agreement, with its significance for Northern Ireland.
 Šefčovič said the summit will also be a chance to look at sectoral issues, pointing to last year’s progress on fisheries, energy and Erasmus+.
 “We aim to complete negotiations on a common sanitary and phytosanitary area, a linkage between our emissions trading systems and the creation of a youth experience scheme as a package for the summit, ” he said.
 He said there are also ongoing talks about the UK’s participation in the EU’s internal electricity market, and “an appropriate financial contribution from the UK towards the reducing economic, social and territorial disparities between regions in the union.”
 The summit will also look at foreign policy issues, given the EU and the UK’s continued support for Ukraine.
 He added that “given the geopolitical context, which is much changed since the withdrawal of the UK from the EU,” there is also scope for more work on supporting integrated value chains between the EU and the UK.
 Share 16m ago 05.29 EDT 'What we saw on Saturday was really an exceptional level of violence' - The Latest
 For a good summary of where we are when it comes to the French protests, you can catch up with Jon Henley’s commentary for The Latest. 
 “ What we saw on Saturday was really an exceptional level of violence, even by French standards. In several towns and cities, there were attacks on those institutional targets. … 
 If this kind of violence continues, then that’s clearly a message that’s going to start appealing to more and more French voters. 
 10:46 France protests escalate with riots, looting and 2,400 arrests - The Latest Share 50m ago 04.54 EDT French PM Lecornu to meet political leaders this week
 Facing growing political pressure over the protests and riots, France’s PM Sébastien Lecornu will convene political parties for a meeting on Thursday , a member of his team said.
 The conversation is also likely to touch upon the issue of policing, with critics saying the initial response to the protests was too heavy-handed.
 View image in fullscreen France's prime minister Sébastien Lecornu leave an emergency meeting, with his ministers behind Photograph: Julien de Rosa/Reuters He will also meet with trade unions on Wednesday.
 The government has come under criticism from parties across the political spectrum, with far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen describing the unrest as a “wake-up call” that exposed a “profound crisis” of authority.
 Share 1h ago 04.29 EDT Macron secures additional diesel deliveries from the Gulf in bid to lower prices at home
 Meanwhile, president Emmanuel Macron has secured the delivery of an additional 200,000 tonnes of diesel per month from the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain during a tour of the Gulf, the French presidency said.
 View image in fullscreen The Emir of Kuwait Sheik Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah welcomes French President Emmanuel Macron to Kuwait. Photograph: Benoit Tessier-Pool/SIPA/Shutterstock With the addition of deliveries from Saudi Arabia, France has commitments for 295,000 tonnes per month, representing just over 10 percent of its consumption, the presidency added.
 Macron is undertaking a tour of key energy suppliers in the Gulf in an effort to secure oil and diesel supplies and bring down prices in France, after a weekend of violent protests sparked by soaring living costs.
 Share 2h ago 03.56 EDT 40-year-old man arrested in relation to Limoges town hall fire
 A 40-year-old man was arrested on Tuesday on suspicion of being involved in the arson attack that ravaged Limoges town hall over the weekend, French media reported. 
 View image in fullscreen A fire burning and destroying the city hall after a group of individuals forced entry into the building during ongoing protest action against the "high cost of living", in Limoges, central France. Photograph: Pascal Lachenaud/AFP/Getty Images The man is reportedly a “far-left activist” with a prior record that saw him placed on the security services’ watchlist, according to Le Figaro. 
 Share 2h ago 03.37 EDT Morning opening: French PM says targeted curfews 'have contributed to calm overnight'
 Jakub Krupa French prime minister Sébastien Lecornu said that targeted curfews introduced in parts of Paris and other major cities “have contributed to calm overnight,” as he suggested more curfews could be introduced if needed today. 
 View image in fullscreen A police helicopter overflies the Place de la République during the first night of an enforced overnight curfew following recent widespread urban unrest in France. Photograph: CLPRESS/ABACA/Shutterstock In a particular symbol of stepped up security measures, a helicopter flew over the French capital’s Place de la Republique, one of the epicentres of the unrest, sweeping a powerful searchlight across the square, AFP said.
 While some restrictions, such as those in Paris, initially applied only for the night from Monday to Tuesday, others, particularly in Bordeaux and Nice, were set to remain in force for several days, the agency noted.
 Meanwhile, Italy’s government decided to dispatch 500 army troops to Milan after two days of unrest in the city, with shops in the city centre affected by riots and looting.
 View image in fullscreen Empty storefronts and closed high-fashion boutiques in the fashion district and on Via Montenapoleone in Milan, Italy. Photograph: Emanuele Roberto De Carli/NurPhoto/Shutterstock I will keep an eye on the latest from both France and Italy. 
 Elsewhere, the European parliament in Strasbourg will debate EU-UK relations this morning , and Nato’s Mark Rutte will host the Turkish foreign minister for talks. Lithuania’s president Gitanas Nausėda is in Poland to discuss regional security.
 I will bring you all the key news from across Europe here.
 It’s Tuesday, 20 October 2026 , it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live .
 Good morning.
